name: Betaine

angle.text: Users take betaine as a training supplement, hoping for more strength and power and a fuller, better-hydrated muscle look. Small trials have measured strength and body composition, with mixed results. Claims about cortisol and overtraining rest mostly on limited or anecdotal reports.

summary: Studied for strength, power, and body composition.
currentQuick:
Betaine, also called trimethylglycine, is a small compound found in beets, spinach, wheat and shellfish. It is also produced in the body from choline and sold as a supplement for sports use.
Studies have looked at strength, power and body composition. A meta-analysis suggests a small gain in maximal strength, mainly lower body, while evidence for body composition and power is inconsistent.
How it works: Betaine acts as an osmolyte that protects cells under stress and as a methyl donor, converting homocysteine to methionine. Proposed performance effects include better cell hydration, creatine synthesis support and effects on anabolic signalling, though human data are limited.
Risks and caveats: Betaine is legal and has low acute toxicity. Gastrointestinal upset and a fishy odor can occur, and it may raise cholesterol in some people. It is a prescription medicine for homocystinuria; betaine hydrochloride sold for digestion is a different product. Published trials are small and short.
deepLead:
Betaine, also called trimethylglycine (TMG) or glycine betaine, is a small N-trimethylated amino acid derivative first isolated from sugar beets, after which it is named . It occurs in beets, spinach, quinoa, wheat and seafood, is made in the body from choline, and acts both as a methyl donor in one-carbon metabolism and as an osmolyte that protects cells under stress .
As a sports supplement, betaine anhydrous is taken by lifters in the hope of improving strength, power and body composition; it appears in pre-workout powders and is marketed with claims about cell hydration, cortisol and recovery .
Human trials on exercise performance are small and short, with some reporting benefits and others reporting none . A separate pharmaceutical betaine is prescribed for homocystinuria . The term 'betaine' also covers a chemical class, and betaine hydrochloride sold for digestion is a different product .

name: Ashwagandha

angle.text: Ashwagandha is taken as an adaptogen to lower stress, improve sleep and nudge testosterone, so that users recover and train harder in pursuit of a more muscular physique. Small human trials report modest changes in strength, stress scores and some hormone readings; visible appearance changes have not been directly studied.

summary: Adaptogen with small bumps to strength, stress, and some hormone readings.
currentQuick:
Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) is a shrub whose root is a staple of Ayurvedic medicine. Extracts are marketed as adaptogens for stress, sleep and vitality.
In fitness use it is taken to support strength, recovery and testosterone. Small randomized trials report modest gains in strength and some hormone readings; the samples are small and funding is often industry-linked, and the wiki's rating is moderate.
How it works: The active constituents are withanolides, which appear to modulate the stress axis, lower cortisol and affect GABAergic and inflammatory signalling. Researchers suggest any effect on muscle likely comes indirectly through improved stress, sleep and recovery rather than direct anabolism.
Risks and caveats: Ashwagandha is sold as a supplement in most countries. Rare cases of liver injury have been reported, and it can affect thyroid hormone levels and cause drowsiness or stomach upset. It is generally avoided in pregnancy and may interact with thyroid, sedative and immunosuppressant drugs.
deepLead:
Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera), also called Indian ginseng or winter cherry, is an evergreen shrub of the nightshade family whose root powder has been used for centuries in traditional Indian medicine . It is sold as a dietary supplement as root or leaf powder or standardized extracts, marketed as an adaptogen for stress, sleep, vitality, strength and testosterone .
The main phytochemicals are withanolides, steroidal lactones such as withaferin A, which are structurally similar to ginsenosides, giving rise to the nickname 'Indian ginseng' . In fitness communities it is used for recovery, stress and testosterone support, often alongside other herbal products .
Meta-analyses of randomised trials report reductions in stress and anxiety scores and a small effect on sleep, but with substantial heterogeneity . Wikipedia states that current clinical evidence is insufficient to confirm safety or efficacy and notes rare cases of liver injury . A few small trials have examined strength, recovery and endurance outcomes .

name: Turkesterone

angle.text: Turkesterone is promoted to bodybuilders as a natural alternative to anabolic steroids, with users hoping for muscle growth without suppressing their own hormones. Human evidence for muscle gain is largely absent; supporting claims come mainly from animal and cell studies, sellers' marketing and anecdote.

summary: Hyped ecdysteroid marketed as anabolic. Human evidence is weak.
currentQuick:
Turkesterone is a phytoecdysteroid, a plant steroid structurally related to insect molting hormones, first isolated from Ajuga turkestanica. It became popular in supplements as a purported natural anabolic.
Claims rest largely on rodent studies and on research into the better-known ecdysterone. Human trials of turkesterone specifically are small and mostly have not shown meaningful muscle or strength benefits; the wiki's rating is limited.
How it works: In animals, ecdysteroids appear to increase muscle protein synthesis, possibly via estrogen receptor beta and signalling pathways, rather than through the androgen receptor. How well turkesterone is absorbed and whether these findings apply to people are unresolved.
Risks and caveats: It is sold as a dietary supplement in the US, with unresolved novel-food status in the EU. Short-term human studies have not reported serious harm, but long-term data are lacking, and independent testing has found products containing far less turkesterone than labelled.
deepLead:
Turkesterone is a naturally occurring phytoecdysteroid, a plant steroid related to the molting hormones of insects, found in Ajuga turkestanica and several other plants, including Vitex species, Cyanotis arachnoidea, wheat and Rhaponticum acaule . It is sold as a dietary supplement and promoted to bodybuilders as a natural anabolic, often described by sellers as an alternative to anabolic steroids .
Most of the supporting claims come from animal and cell research and from work on the related compound ecdysterone . Wikipedia states that turkesterone is under laboratory research for anabolic effects through PI3K and AKT signalling and that its pharmacokinetics, bioavailability and effects in humans remain to be determined .
Human data specific to turkesterone are limited to small short-term studies. A 2024 preliminary study of acute doses in 11 men found no significant effects on IGF-1, resting metabolic rate or lipid and carbohydrate metabolism . The compound is not an androgen in the usual sense; proponents describe an estrogen receptor beta-linked or non-androgenic route, a view that appears in forum discussion .

name: Ecdysterone

angle.text: Ecdysterone is taken by lifters as a plant-derived anabolic, with some users promoting it as a hormone-neutral way to add muscle. One small human trial reported greater muscle gain with training, and cell and animal studies point to estrogen receptor beta; evidence is preliminary and product quality is a recurring concern.

summary: Plant/insect steroid with early hypertrophy signals. Preliminary.
currentQuick:
Ecdysterone, or 20-hydroxyecdysone, is the main molting hormone of insects and crustaceans and is also found in plants such as spinach and Cyanotis. It is sold as a supplement and is being developed as an investigational drug for some muscle conditions.
A widely cited study in young men reported greater muscle gains with high-dose ecdysterone alongside training; replication is lacking and other findings are mixed, so the evidence is considered preliminary.
How it works: In rodents ecdysterone stimulates muscle protein synthesis without androgen receptor activity, with evidence pointing to estrogen receptor beta and downstream Akt signalling. Human mechanism data are limited.
Risks and caveats: Acute toxicity appears low. It is sold as a supplement, but the World Anti-Doping Agency has monitored it, and product purity is reported to be variable. Long-term human safety has not been established.
deepLead:
Ecdysterone, more formally 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E), is a naturally occurring ecdysteroid hormone that controls molting and metamorphosis in insects and crustaceans; it is also produced by plants such as Cyanotis vaga, Ajuga turkestanica and Rhaponticum carthamoides, where it is thought to defend against herbivores . Spinach and quinoa are listed among dietary sources .
Mammals lack the arthropod ecdysone receptor, but ecdysterone still affects mammalian systems, and in mammals it is hypothesised to bind estrogen receptor beta (ERbeta) . It is sold as a supplement for bodybuilding and sport and is also being developed as an investigational compound for muscle-related conditions .
Research on its anabolic effects in people is limited. A 2006 study concluded that a modest oral amount did not significantly affect training adaptations, while a 2019 controlled study funded by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) reported larger increases in muscle mass and bench press performance with ecdysterone than without . Replication evidence is sparse.

name: Testosterone

chain: Leaner, more masculine physique and face
angle.text: Testosterone is discussed in looksmaxxing circles both as the hormone behind masculine features (muscle, jaw and brow development, body hair, voice) and as a therapy (TRT) or high-level drug for physique. Its muscle effects are well studied in medical and trial settings; claims about enhancing facial structure in adults are mostly anecdotal.

summary: The androgen. Muscle protein synthesis, bone density, male secondary characteristics.
note: Strong in diagnosed deficiency; serious risks outside indicated treatment.
currentQuick:
Testosterone is the principal male sex hormone, an androgen produced mainly in the testes. It drives male secondary sexual characteristics, bone density, red blood cell production and muscle mass.
In medicine it is prescribed to treat diagnosed hypogonadism. Healthy young men given supraphysiologic doses gain muscle in a dose-dependent way, and anabolic steroid use is a feature of physique culture. Evidence of benefit is strong where there is true deficiency; use beyond that is associated with serious documented risks.
How it works: Testosterone binds the androgen receptor, increasing muscle protein synthesis, satellite cell activity and bone formation, and is partly converted to estradiol and dihydrotestosterone, which have their own effects.
Risks and caveats: It is a prescription-only, controlled substance in many countries. Documented risks include suppression of natural production and fertility, acne, polycythemia, blood pressure and lipid changes, mood effects and possible cardiovascular strain; abrupt cessation can leave a deficiency. This entry is informational and not guidance for use.
deepLead:
Testosterone is the principal male sex hormone and an androgen, a steroid hormone made mainly by the testicles in males and in smaller amounts by the ovaries in females. It drives the development of male reproductive tissues and secondary sexual characteristics, including increases in muscle and bone mass, body hair growth, voice deepening and remodelling of the jaw, brow and facial bone contours at puberty, and it also influences mood, libido, red blood cell production and metabolism.
As a medicine, testosterone is prescribed as replacement therapy for male hypogonadism (a diagnosed deficiency), for gender dysphoria and for some breast cancers, and it appears on the World Health Organization's list of essential medicines. It can be delivered by injection, skin gel or patch, cheek tablet, nasal gel, subdermal pellet or oral capsule. Outside medicine, supraphysiologic doses are a staple of bodybuilding and physique culture, and testosterone is discussed on strength-training forums such as T Nation, where members talk about both prescribed replacement and wider use of anabolic compounds.
Research supports benefit from replacement in men with true deficiency, with benefit most clearly documented for sexual function, and a large randomized trial in men with hypogonadism found no excess of major cardiovascular events over placebo. name: Somatropin

angle.text: Users take synthetic growth hormone for muscle, fat loss, anti-ageing and, in bodybuilding circles, a so-called steroid look with wider jaw and face. It is approved for deficiency states, and its body-composition effects are studied there; use in healthy adults for appearance is off-label and the facial claims are anecdotal.

summary: Growth hormone. Drives IGF-1 signaling and body-composition change.
note: Strong for deficiency. Chronic excess reshapes faces — pathologically (acromegaly).
currentQuick:
Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone, identical in sequence to the pituitary hormone. It is a prescription medicine for children and adults with growth hormone deficiency and several other conditions.
It is also used illicitly for body composition and anti-aging. Evidence is strong in deficiency; in healthy people studies report it can add some lean mass, with limited strength benefit and notable side effects.
How it works: It binds growth hormone receptors and activates JAK2/STAT signalling, which prompts the liver and other tissues to produce IGF-1. The result is growth, fat mobilization and effects on glucose metabolism and fluid balance.
Risks and caveats: Somatropin is prescription-only and banned in sport. Side effects include fluid retention, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and insulin resistance. Chronic excess causes acromegaly, with enlargement of the jaw, brow and hands, plus heart and metabolic problems and a possible cancer link. This is informational, not guidance for use.
deepLead:
Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH or HGH), a biosynthetic form of the pituitary hormone whose amino acid sequence matches the natural hormone. It is prescribed to treat growth hormone deficiency in children and adults, and several other conditions involving growth failure or body-composition change, and it has been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for these uses since the mid-1980s.
Outside those indications, growth hormone is used or discussed for muscle, fat loss, recovery and anti-ageing in bodybuilding and physique communities, where it is often described alongside anabolic steroids and insulin. In a 2003 pair of editorials, the New England Journal of Medicine said there was no evidence that HGH is safe and effective in healthy adults or older people, and stressed that the risks of long-term treatment were unknown. Chronic excess of growth hormone occurs in the disease acromegaly, which is described in medical sources by enlargement of bones and soft tissue and is mentioned in forum discussion of facial change.
The evidence base is strongest for children with deficiency, where randomized phase 3 trials have compared daily and weekly preparations, and for adults with diagnosed deficiency, where replacement improves body composition and lipids but a long-term mortality benefit has not been shown.

name: MK-677

chain: Better recovery and sleep, more appetite
angle.text: MK-677 is an oral ghrelin mimic that users take to raise growth hormone for recovery, sleep, bulking and, among younger users, possible height. Trials show raised GH and IGF-1 and some lean-mass change in other populations; an aesthetic benefit is unproven and appetite increase is a known effect.

summary: Oral ghrelin agonist that raises GH and IGF-1 (and hunger). No proven aesthetic benefit.
currentQuick:
MK-677 (ibutamoren) is an orally active, non-peptide drug that mimics ghrelin and raises growth hormone and IGF-1. It was developed by Merck but never approved, and is sold as a research chemical.
Trials in older adults and obese men showed increased fat-free mass but no clear functional improvement, and no cosmetic benefit has been demonstrated; the wiki's rating is unproven.
How it works: It activates the ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a) in the pituitary and hypothalamus, producing pulsatile growth hormone release and downstream IGF-1 elevation, plus increased appetite.
Risks and caveats: Not approved for any use and prohibited in sport. Reported effects include increased appetite, fluid retention, lethargy and reduced insulin sensitivity; a heart failure signal appeared in one trial. Long-term effects of sustained IGF-1 elevation are unknown, and products may be mislabelled.
deepLead:
MK-677, also known as ibutamoren (developmental codes MK-0677, L-163,191 and, in more recent development, LUM-201), is an orally active, non-peptide drug that mimics the hormone ghrelin. By activating the ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a) in the pituitary and hypothalamus, it raises growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels and also raises cortisol and appetite. It was developed by Merck in the 1990s and has never been approved for any indication; it remains an investigational compound.
Human trials in older adults, obese men, dieting volunteers and patients recovering from hip fracture have shown that it increases GH and IGF-1 and increases fat-free mass, while studies for functional benefit, Alzheimer's disease and frailty have not shown clear clinical gains, and a heart-failure safety signal was reported in a hip-fracture trial. Reported adverse effects include increased appetite, fluid retention, lethargy and reduced insulin sensitivity.
MK-677 is sold online as a research chemical, discussed on bodybuilding and physique forums as an oral alternative to injectable growth hormone or peptides, and prohibited in sport. No trial has tested it for cosmetic or aesthetic outcomes in healthy people.

name: CJC-1295

angle.text: CJC-1295 is an injectable peptide that users take to raise growth hormone for recovery, fat loss, skin and sleep, and some younger users hope for height. Human data are limited to a few endocrine studies showing raised GH and IGF-1; the appearance claims are untested and rest on anecdote.

summary: GHRH analogue that pushes growth hormone release. Limited human endocrine data.
currentQuick:
CJC-1295 is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone releasing hormone developed in the early 2000s. The long-acting version binds albumin, extending its half-life.
Early human studies showed raised growth hormone and IGF-1, but development stopped and no data show a muscle or cosmetic benefit; the wiki's rating is unproven.
How it works: It binds the GHRH receptor on pituitary somatotrophs, increasing growth hormone secretion and IGF-1 levels for days after a single administration in the long-acting form.
Risks and caveats: It is not an approved medicine, is sold as a research peptide, and is banned in sport. A phase II trial was halted after a death in a participant. Reported effects include flushing, headache, water retention and injection-site reactions. Long-term safety is unknown and the regulatory status of compounded versions has been in flux.
deepLead:
CJC-1295 is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH, also called growth hormone-releasing factor) developed by ConjuChem Biotechnologies. In its best-known form, CJC-1295 with a 'drug affinity complex' (DAC), the peptide attaches to the blood protein albumin, which extends its half-life to roughly six to eight days and allows a single injection to raise growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) for days. A shorter-acting version without the DAC, often called 'modified GRF (1-29)', is a separate compound, though the two are sometimes confused.
Human trials in healthy adults showed prolonged GH and IGF-1 stimulation, but development for lipodystrophy in people with HIV and for growth hormone deficiency ended after a phase II trial was halted following the death of a participant. The attending physician thought the death was most likely due to previously undiagnosed coronary artery disease and unrelated to the drug, but the research was stopped as a precaution. No published trial has shown muscle, fat-loss or cosmetic benefit from CJC-1295 in healthy people.
CJC-1295 is not an approved medicine. It is sold as a research peptide and reported by forum users as prescribed by some clinics, often combined with the ghrelin-mimetic ipamorelin, and it is prohibited in sport. Recent reviews of peptide use in sport and aesthetics describe human evidence as scarce and note risks associated with mislabeled or contaminated products.

name: Ipamorelin

chain: Possible growth while plates are open
angle.text: Ipamorelin is a GH-releasing peptide that users, often teenagers or young adults, take hoping for height, better sleep, recovery and facial bone growth, frequently alongside CJC-1295. Human data are thin and focused on GH release; the height and facial claims are untested and largely anecdotal.

summary: Selective GH secretagogue; thin human data.
currentQuick:
Ipamorelin is a synthetic pentapeptide that selectively stimulates growth hormone release. Novo Nordisk developed it in the 1990s, and it is now sold as a research peptide.
Clinical work has been limited, mainly early pharmacology and a trial in post-surgical bowel recovery that showed no clear benefit. Good human data supporting claims for muscle and fat loss have not been published.
How it works: It is a selective agonist of the ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a), triggering pulsatile pituitary growth hormone release with relatively little effect on cortisol and prolactin compared with older secretagogues.
Risks and caveats: It is not approved for human use and is banned in sport. Short-term data are limited; theoretical concerns include insulin resistance, fluid retention and effects of long-term GH/IGF-1 elevation. Product quality is unregulated.
deepLead:
Ipamorelin (development code NNC 26-0161) is a synthetic pentapeptide that stimulates the release of growth hormone (GH) by acting as a selective agonist at the ghrelin receptor, also called the growth hormone secretagogue receptor. It was derived from the earlier compound GHRP-1 and originally developed by Novo Nordisk in the 1990s.
It was described in 1998 as the first selective GH secretagogue because, unlike older peptides such as GHRP-6 and GHRP-2, it raises GH without a notable rise in cortisol or ACTH, and it does not affect prolactin, FSH, LH or TSH. Clinical development, led by Helsinn Therapeutics, focused on postoperative ileus (a post-surgical bowel dysfunction) and was discontinued for lack of efficacy.
Ipamorelin is not an approved medicine. It is sold as a research peptide, used by some athletes and physique enthusiasts, and prohibited in sport. Reviews of peptides used in sport and aesthetic medicine describe human evidence of cosmetic or performance benefit as limited, with most data coming from short-term pharmacology studies and animal work.

name: Sermorelin

angle.text: Sermorelin is a GHRH analogue that users take hoping to raise growth hormone for height in teenagers, leanness, sleep and anti-ageing. It was approved in the past for diagnosing and treating GH deficiency in children; its use for cosmetic or height goals in healthy people is off-label and untested.

summary: GHRH analogue stimulating your own GH release. Hormonal mechanism is real; cosmetic benefit unproven.
currentQuick:
Sermorelin is a synthetic fragment of growth hormone releasing hormone consisting of its first 29 amino acids. It was FDA-approved for diagnosing and treating growth hormone deficiency in children before manufacturing ceased in 2008.
It is still available through compounding pharmacies and used off-label for age-related decline. Its hormonal mechanism is documented, while evidence for visible body-composition or cosmetic benefit is limited.
How it works: It acts on GHRH receptors in the pituitary to prompt natural, pulsatile growth hormone release, so the body's feedback mechanisms still operate, unlike with injected GH.
Risks and caveats: It is prescription-only in the US and banned in competitive sport. Common effects are injection-site reactions, flushing and headache. It is avoided with active cancer and in pregnancy. Quality of compounded preparations and the claims made in telehealth marketing are reported to vary.
deepLead:
Sermorelin (sermorelin acetate; brand names Geref and Gerel) is a synthetic peptide made of the first 29 amino acids of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), thought to be the shortest fully active fragment of the natural 44-amino-acid hormone. It binds the GHRH receptor on the pituitary gland and prompts release of the body's own growth hormone (GH).
The US Food and Drug Administration approved sermorelin in 1997 as a diagnostic agent for growth hormone secretion and as a treatment for children with growth hormone deficiency or growth failure. The manufacturer discontinued production in 2008 for commercial reasons not related to safety, and it is no longer available as an approved commercial product, though it can still be obtained through compounding pharmacies and prescribed off label.
In recent years sermorelin has been promoted by telehealth and wellness clinics for age-related decline, body composition and recovery. Reviews describe its hormonal mechanism as real but note limited controlled evidence of visible body-composition or cosmetic benefit in healthy adults, and it is prohibited in competitive sport.

name: GHRP-6

angle.text: GHRP-6 is a GH-releasing peptide that users take to raise growth hormone for muscle, recovery and fat loss, and for the strong hunger it causes, which some use to aid bulking. It has been studied in humans for GH release; the effect on physique is untested and anecdotal.

summary: GH secretagogue that also makes you ravenous.
currentQuick:
GHRP-6 is a synthetic hexapeptide from the first generation of growth hormone releasing peptides. It was a research tool in the 1980s and 1990s and is now sold as a research chemical.
It is known for raising growth hormone and also for a strong hunger effect. Human evidence of improved muscle or appearance has not been published.
How it works: GHRP-6 activates the ghrelin receptor, causing growth hormone release and appetite stimulation, and also raises cortisol and prolactin somewhat.
Risks and caveats: It is not approved for human use and is banned in sport. Reported effects include intense hunger, water retention and flushing. Long-term safety is unknown and quality is unregulated.
deepLead:
GHRP-6 (growth hormone-releasing peptide 6, developmental code SKF-110679) is a synthetic hexapeptide with the sequence His-D-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2. It belongs to a family of met-enkephalin analogues containing unnatural D-amino acids that lack opioid activity but strongly stimulate growth hormone (GH) release, and it was the first hexapeptide extensively studied in humans.
GHRP-6 acts through a receptor distinct from the one used by growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH). That receptor, originally named the growth hormone secretagogue receptor, is now recognised as the ghrelin receptor, which is why GHRP-6 is described as a synthetic ghrelin mimetic. In addition to releasing GH, it stimulates appetite and raises cortisol, ACTH and prolactin to some degree.
GHRP-6 has been used mainly as a research and diagnostic tool, including in provocative tests for adult GH deficiency, and it is sold as a research chemical to bodybuilders and others. It is not approved as a treatment, is prohibited in sport, and no published trial has shown improved muscle or appearance in healthy people.

name: IGF-1 LR3

angle.text: IGF-1 LR3 is an injectable growth-factor analogue sold to bodybuilders for muscle growth and healing, sometimes stacked with insulin or steroids. Reliable human evidence for muscle gain is lacking; claims about local injection growth, bloat and detectability come from forums and vendors.

summary: Modified IGF-1 analogue sold for muscle growth. No reliable human evidence.
currentQuick:
IGF-1 LR3 is a lab-modified version of insulin-like growth factor 1 with an extended amino acid chain and an arginine substitution. It was developed for cell culture and sold to bodybuilders as an injectable research chemical.
Animal and cell data show growth effects, but no reliable human trials of benefit in healthy people have been published.
How it works: It activates the IGF-1 receptor and downstream PI3K/Akt/mTOR signalling. The modifications lower binding to IGF binding proteins, so it stays active longer than native IGF-1.
Risks and caveats: Not approved for humans and banned in sport. Main concerns are low blood sugar, fluid retention, joint pain and organ growth, plus theoretical cancer promotion. Products are unregulated.
deepLead:
IGF-1 LR3 (long arginine 3 insulin-like growth factor 1, also written LR3-IGF-1 or Long R3 IGF-1) is a synthetic, lengthened analogue of human insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1). It differs from the natural hormone by an arginine in place of glutamic acid at position 3 and an extra 13 amino acids at the N-terminus, giving a protein of 83 amino acids compared with 70 for native IGF-1.
These changes leave it able to activate the IGF-1 receptor while sharply reducing its binding to the IGF-binding proteins that normally restrain IGF-1 in the blood. As a result, Wikipedia reports it is roughly three times as potent as IGF-1 and has a half-life of about 20 to 30 hours, compared with about 12 to 15 hours for IGF-1. In bodybuilding forums it is discussed as an injectable compound used alongside other agents.
IGF-1 LR3 is not an approved drug, and no published human trial has tested it for muscle growth, appearance or other benefit in healthy people. Evidence for its effects comes from cell and animal studies of IGF-1 signalling, and it falls under anti-doping rules covering growth factors.

name: Follistatin-344

angle.text: Follistatin-344 is an unapproved injectable sold to people hoping to block myostatin and build muscle beyond natural limits. The protein has been studied in animals and in gene-therapy research, but injected vendor products are untested for this use in humans; food and training claims are mostly anecdotal.

summary: The myostatin-blocker dream. Experimental only.
currentQuick:
Follistatin-344 refers to a form of the protein follistatin (the 344 label is used by peptide vendors) sold as an experimental myostatin blocker. Follistatin is a natural protein that binds and neutralizes myostatin and activins.
Gene therapy work in animals and early clinical trials shows muscle effects, but no credible human evidence exists for injected peptide products.
How it works: Follistatin binds myostatin and activin, preventing them from signalling through their receptors, which relieves the brake on muscle growth in animal models.
Risks and caveats: Not approved; banned in sport. Because follistatin affects reproductive hormones and other tissues, blocking these pathways raises theoretical concerns. Marketed peptides are unregulated and may not contain what is claimed.
deepLead:
Follistatin-344 (often written FS-344) is the label under which unapproved, injectable preparations of the protein follistatin are sold by peptide vendors, mainly to people interested in building muscle. Follistatin itself is a secreted glycoprotein encoded by the FST gene in humans; it binds and neutralizes members of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta) superfamily, notably activin and myostatin (also called GDF-8), a protein that limits muscle growth.
The appeal of the product in bodybuilding and looksmaxxing circles rests on animal research in which blocking myostatin, either by gene knockout or by raising follistatin levels, produced larger muscles. Human work with follistatin has so far consisted of gene-therapy studies, in which a viral vector or plasmid delivers the follistatin gene, rather than injections of a purified peptide. A 2026 narrative review of peptides marketed directly to patients for musculoskeletal injury and athletic performance included FS-344 among unapproved compounds and concluded that for many such peptides, favourable results come from animal models while rigorous human safety data are scarce.
FS-344 is not approved as a medicine in any major jurisdiction, and community discussion of it on forums such as T Nation is mostly speculative about its effects and side effects.

name: Ostarine

chain: Lean mass gain, some fat loss
angle.text: Ostarine is a SARM used by lifters for lean mass and a leaner look, sometimes alongside TRT or after steroid cycles. It has been trialled for muscle wasting and showed lean-mass gains in those settings; use for aesthetics is off-label, and hormone suppression is a documented effect.

summary: The most-studied SARM; never approved. Suppresses your own hormones.
currentQuick:
Ostarine (enobosarm, MK-2866) is a nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator developed to treat muscle wasting. It reached phase III trials but was never approved.
Trials showed lean mass gains without matching functional gains. Recreational use is common and a frequent cause of anti-doping violations.
How it works: It binds the androgen receptor, aiming for activity in muscle and bone with less effect on tissues such as the prostate. It suppresses natural testosterone production.
Risks and caveats: Not approved and banned in sport. Reported harms include hormonal suppression, lipid changes and drug-induced liver injury. Gray-market products are often mislabelled.
deepLead:
Ostarine, known in the medical literature as enobosarm and by the code names GTx-024, MK-2866 and S-22, is an orally taken, nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM). Developed to treat muscle wasting, it was tested in cancer cachexia, sarcopenia and other conditions, and it is not approved as a medicine for any use. The name Ostarine was a tentative brand name chosen by its developer, GTx, Inc., that was never used commercially but persists as a synonym; enobosarm is the International Nonproprietary Name.
In late-stage trials in people with lung cancer, enobosarm increased lean body mass but did not consistently improve physical function, and development for muscle wasting in cancer ended without approval. Development has continued for other uses, including androgen receptor-positive breast cancer and, according to Wikipedia, preserving body composition in people taking GLP-1 receptor agonists such as semaglutide.
Outside medicine, ostarine is sold online as a research chemical or gym supplement and is widely discussed on bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums as a milder alternative to anabolic steroids. Reported adverse effects in trials include lowered HDL cholesterol and testosterone and raised liver enzymes, and case reports describe drug-induced liver injury. A 2017 JAMA analysis of products marketed online as SARMs examined their chemical identity and labelling, reflecting concern about the composition of such products. The compound is prohibited in spor

name: LGD-4033

angle.text: LGD-4033 is a SARM used by lifters to add lean mass in a few weeks with less perceived hormonal impact than steroids. Small trials in older and young men showed lean-mass gains alongside hormonal suppression and lipid changes; evidence for aesthetic use is limited, and product mislabelling is a reported issue.

summary: SARM; lean mass gains in small trials, hormonal suppression in practice.
currentQuick:
LGD-4033 (ligandrol) is a nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator investigated for muscle wasting. A phase I study found increased lean mass in healthy men, but development stalled.
It is widely sold as a research chemical. Small trials show lean mass gains, and observations of recreational use report hormone and lipid problems.
How it works: It selectively activates the androgen receptor in muscle and bone and suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, lowering natural testosterone.
Risks and caveats: Not approved and banned in sport. Documented problems include testosterone suppression, reduced HDL cholesterol and drug-induced liver injury, especially at doses above trial levels. Product contents are unreliable.

LGD-4033, also called Ligandrol and by the developmental code VK5211, is an orally taken, nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) originally developed by Ligand Pharmaceuticals. It has been studied for muscle atrophy, including after hip fracture, and was also explored for cachexia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis; it is not approved for any medical use.
In a randomised phase I trial in 76 healthy men, 21 days of LGD-4033 was well tolerated and raised lean body mass, and a later phase 2 trial in people recovering from hip fracture reported dose-dependent increases in lean mass. The compound has far fewer published human studies than the SARM enobosarm, with only four small clinical studies reported as of 2023 according to Wikipedia.
LGD-4033 is also sold online as a research chemical and discussed on bodybuilding forums. Published concerns include dose-dependent drops in testosterone and HDL cholesterol in trials, multiple case reports of drug-induced liver injury in non-medical users, and a JAMA analysis of products sold online as SARMs that examined their composition and labelling. The compound is on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list.

name: RAD-140

angle.text: RAD-140 is a potent SARM used by lifters for muscle and fat loss, with some hoping for less suppression than steroids. It has been studied in animals and is under development for breast cancer; human evidence for physique use is lacking, with liver and hormone effects reported.

summary: Potent SARM with liver and hormone risks. Insufficient evidence it is safe.
currentQuick:
RAD-140 (testolone) is a nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator developed by Radius Health, studied in preclinical models for muscle and breast cancer. It has never completed human efficacy trials.
It is sold as a research chemical for muscle gain, with little human data.
How it works: It binds the androgen receptor with tissue selectivity and suppresses natural androgen production.
Risks and caveats: Not approved and banned in sport. Case reports link it to drug-induced liver injury, and it suppresses hormones. Evidence of its safety is insufficient. Products may be mislabelled.

RAD-140, whose International Nonproprietary Name is vosilasarm and which is also called RAD140, EP0062 and by the black-market name Testolone, is an orally taken, nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM). It was developed by Radius Health in 2010, first described in the literature in 2011, and is now under development by Ellipses Pharma for androgen receptor-positive, estrogen receptor-negative, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer. Earlier plans to develop it for sarcopenia, osteoporosis and cancer cachexia were discontinued.
No human data on its effect on lean body mass have been published as of 2022 according to Wikipedia; the only completed human trial was a small first-in-human phase 1 study in postmenopausal women with breast cancer. Animal studies in rats and monkeys showed muscle-stimulating effects with weaker effects on the prostate, which is the basis of its tissue-selective label.
RAD-140 is sold online for physique and performance purposes and is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's prohibited list. Published case reports describe drug-induced liver injury, myocarditis and heart failure in people who used it non-medically, and Wikipedia notes that many products sold online as a specific SARM contain none of it or unrelated substances.

name: YK-11

angle.text: YK-11 is a steroid-like compound sold as a myostatin-inhibiting SARM, which users take hoping for gains beyond ordinary SARMs. Evidence is limited to cell and animal work; reliable human studies of muscle gain are absent, and its classification is itself disputed.

summary: Marketed as a myostatin-inhibiting SARM. No reliable human evidence.
currentQuick:
YK-11 is an experimental steroid-based compound classed as a SARM, though it behaves as a partial androgen receptor agonist. Research is confined to cell studies, mainly from Japanese groups in 2011 to 2013.
It is sold as a research chemical. No human trials exist.
How it works: In cultured muscle cells it increased follistatin expression and reduced myostatin signalling via androgen receptor activation. These results have not been shown in humans.
Risks and caveats: Not approved and banned in sport. Safety is untested in humans, and liver, hormonal and cardiovascular effects are suspected. Products sold online are frequently mislabelled.
deepLead:
YK-11 is a synthetic steroidal compound that is usually classed as a selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM). Wikipedia describes it as a gene-selective partial agonist of the androgen receptor that does not trigger the N/C interaction normally needed for full receptor activation, and as having anabolic activity in cultured C2C12 myoblasts greater than that of dihydrotestosterone (DHT). It has been investigated in animal studies of sepsis-induced muscle wasting and has appeared on the market as a designer drug.
The compound was reported by Yuichiro Kanno and colleagues at Toho University, Japan, around 2011, with a follow-up 2013 paper in Biological and Pharmaceutical Bulletin reporting that YK-11 increased follistatin expression in myoblasts, the basis of its marketing as a myostatin inhibitor. Published work consists of cell and animal studies; no human clinical trial of YK-11 was found.
YK-11 is not authorised as a medicine anywhere noted in the sources. Health Canada warned in 2022 that SARMs such as YK-11 are not authorised for any use and that bodybuilding products containing them can pose risks such as heart attack, stroke and liver damage. It is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's prohibited list and has been detected in doping control samples and in dietary supplements.

name: Finasteride

angle.text: Finasteride is an approved oral drug that lowers DHT, used in looksmaxxing circles to stop male pattern hair loss and keep the hairline. It is well studied for this use in men; reported sexual and mood side effects, including persistent ones, are a major point of debate, as are lower and topical regimens.

summary: Blocks DHT (type II 5-AR). The proven hair-loss stopper.
note: Can cause sexual and mood side effects in a minority.
currentQuick:
Finasteride is an oral inhibitor of the type II and III isoforms of 5-alpha-reductase, the enzyme that converts testosterone into dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Approved at 1 mg daily as Propecia for male pattern hair loss and at 5 mg as Proscar for benign prostatic hyperplasia, it is the most established medical treatment for slowing androgenetic alopecia.
In trials most men maintain or regrow some hair over several years, with the benefit lost within months of stopping. It is a core component of hair-loss protocols in looksmaxxing and hair-loss communities, usually paired with minoxidil.
How it works: Hair loss in androgenetic alopecia is driven by DHT acting on genetically sensitive scalp follicles, which shrink and spend less time in the growth phase. Finasteride lowers serum DHT by roughly 70 percent and scalp DHT by a similar amount, reducing miniaturisation and allowing some follicles to recover.
Risks and caveats: Decreased libido, erectile dysfunction and ejaculatory problems occur in a minority, and depression and anxiety have been reported. Some men describe persistent sexual or mood symptoms after stopping (post-finasteride syndrome), a condition regulators have noted but whose frequency and cause remain debated. It can affect PSA readings, is contraindicated in pregnancy because of fetal risk, and women should not handle crushed tablets. It is prescription-only.
deepLead:
Finasteride, sold under brand names including Proscar and Propecia, is an oral medication used to treat male pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). It is a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor, an antiandrogen that lowers production of dihydrotestosterone (DHT) by about 70 percent in serum and 65 to 70 percent in scalp skin, according to Wikipedia. The US label describes it as a competitive and specific inhibitor of type II 5-alpha-reductase and indicates the 1 mg hair-loss product for men only.
In randomised trials and meta-analyses, 1 mg daily finasteride has outperformed placebo for hair counts and global assessments in men with androgenetic alopecia, and with minoxidil it is one of the two drugs FDA-approved for male pattern hair loss. Wikipedia reports that two meta-analyses found regrowth of about 15 percent and that treatment mainly slows further loss. Benefit depends on continued use.
Adverse effects include decreased libido, erectile dysfunction and ejaculation disorder in a minority; a 2019 meta-analysis of randomised trials found a 1.57-fold relative risk of sexual dysfunction for 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors and 1.66 for finasteride. name: Dutasteride

angle.text: Dutasteride blocks both 5-alpha-reductase types and is used off-label in most countries to stop male pattern hair loss, often as a stronger option than finasteride. It is approved for hair loss in a few countries and has trial data there; reported side effects and topical use are debated.

summary: Blocks both 5-AR isoenzymes — stronger DHT suppression than finasteride.
currentQuick:
Dutasteride (Avodart) is an inhibitor of both type I and type II 5-alpha-reductase, approved for benign prostatic hyperplasia. It is used off-label, and approved for male pattern hair loss in South Korea and Japan, as an alternative to finasteride.
Head-to-head and pooled analyses indicate that dutasteride produces larger increases in hair counts than 1 mg finasteride, particularly at 0.5 mg, though the comparative trial evidence is limited and sexual side effect comparisons are not conclusive.
How it works: By blocking all active 5-alpha-reductase isoenzymes, dutasteride suppresses serum DHT by more than 90 percent, versus around 70 percent for finasteride. Since scalp follicles express type I as well as type II enzyme, this broader blockade is thought to protect more follicles from DHT-driven miniaturisation.
Risks and caveats: Reported adverse effects resemble those of finasteride: reduced libido, erectile and ejaculatory problems, and mood effects in some users. Its very long half-life means effects can persist for weeks after stopping. It is contraindicated in pregnancy and affects PSA, and it is prescription-only. For hair loss it is largely an off-label use in Western markets.
deepLead:
Dutasteride, sold as Avodart among other brands, is an oral medication that inhibits 5-alpha-reductase, the enzyme that converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT). It is FDA-approved for symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and is used off-label for male pattern hair loss in most countries; it is approved for male androgenetic alopecia at 0.5 mg per day in South Korea (2009), Japan (2015) and Taiwan (2016), according to Wikipedia.
Unlike finasteride, which inhibits the type II and III isoenzymes, dutasteride inhibits types I, II and III, and Wikipedia reports it can lower circulating DHT by up to 98 percent versus 65 to 70 percent for finasteride. A phase III trial compared several dutasteride doses with finasteride and placebo in men with androgenetic alopecia, and a systematic review reported an efficacy ranking of dutasteride 0.5 mg above finasteride 1 mg.
Reported adverse effects are mainly sexual (erectile dysfunction, reduced libido, ejaculation disorders) plus breast disorders; a 2019 meta-analysis found a 1.37-fold relative risk of sexual dysfunction with dutasteride that was not statistically significant, with limited trial data. Its elimination half-life of about 4 to 5 weeks means it remains in the body for months after stopping. It is contraindicated in pregnancy and carries an FDA warning relating to high-grade prostate cancer and PSA interpretation.

name: Minoxidil

angle.text: Minoxidil is used to regrow and thicken scalp hair, and many users also apply it to the beard and brows. Topical forms are approved for scalp hair loss; oral low-dose use is off-label with growing trial data, while beard and brow use is less studied.

summary: Grows hair and extends the growth phase. Topical is OTC; low-dose oral is Rx.
currentQuick:
Minoxidil is a vasodilator first developed as an oral antihypertensive and now best known as a topical treatment for androgenetic alopecia, sold as Rogaine and generics in 2 percent and 5 percent solutions and foams. Topical use is over the counter in many countries, while low-dose oral minoxidil is prescribed off-label.
It promotes regrowth and thickening in many users with pattern hair loss and works independently of hormones, so it is typically combined with a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor. Meta-analyses support both topical and low-dose oral forms, and shedding in the first weeks of use is common.
How it works: Minoxidil is converted to its active sulphate form in the follicle by the enzyme SULT1A1. It opens ATP-sensitive potassium channels, and is thought to prolong the growth (anagen) phase, shorten the resting phase and enlarge miniaturised follicles, possibly by affecting blood flow and growth-factor signalling. The precise mechanism is not fully settled, and response varies with follicle enzyme activity.
Risks and caveats: Topical use can cause scalp irritation, dryness and unwanted facial hair, and propylene glycol in some formulations can cause contact dermatitis. Oral low-dose use can cause hypertrichosis, fluid retention, ankle swelling, fast heart rate and dizziness, and requires medical oversight because of cardiovascular effects. Hair gained is lost again if treatment stops. Minoxidil is toxic to cats if ingested.
deepLead:
Minoxidil, sold as Rogaine and Loniten among other brands, is a vasodilator medication used for high blood pressure and for hair loss. Taken orally at high doses it treats severe hypertension, while topical minoxidil, available over the counter as a solution or foam, is used for androgenetic alopecia, and low-dose oral minoxidil is prescribed off-label for hair loss. Topical 2 percent solution and 5 percent solution and foam are FDA-approved for androgenetic alopecia, and oral minoxidil is not FDA-approved for hair loss.
Wikipedia describes the drug as promoting hair growth, but its effects as fully reversible: benefits depend on indefinite use, and after long-term treatment is stopped hair density falls to placebo levels within about 24 weeks. Meta-analyses of randomised trials found 2 percent and 5 percent topical minoxidil superior to placebo in men, and a 2024 randomised trial in JAMA Dermatology compared oral and topical minoxidil in men.
Minoxidil acts independently of androgens, which is why it is frequently discussed alongside 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors such as finasteride. Topical side effects are mainly scalp irritation, itching and unwanted hair growth elsewhere; oral minoxidil can cause fluid retention, rapid heartbeat, dizziness and hypertrichosis, and rare serious events such as pericardial effusion have been described mainly at higher doses.
